I will do it close to what worked for me before, not too fancy. On 5 mu, every bag of fertilizer and every spray costs real money, so I will not gamble, but I also will not cut too hard and lose yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety like the ones people around Quzhou plant when they see good stand and good grain fill. Wheat needs steadier feeding, so I will put most phosphorus in early, give enough nitrogen, and add some potassium because the land gives better if I do not let it go weak. Since I have well water, I will irrigate wheat about 3 times if the season is normal: once after winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around grain filling. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what usually gives better yield here if the stand is even. I will keep maize fertilizer a bit heavier on nitrogen, not too low, because if maize gets hungry in summer the ears stay short and that loss hurts more than spending a little extra. After wheat harvest I will move fast, mostly no-tillage direct seeding or very light work, because timing matters. I will spray wheat about 3 times and maize about 2 times, depending on weeds and insects. I will do about what I did last year, with a small push on balanced fertilizer and keeping irrigation on time, because that is safer than trying something completely new.
